newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish insurance body sees PLN 1 bln flood payouts.
newsitem.headline: Polish insurance body sees PLN 1 bln flood payouts.

text.p: Polish insurance companies will pay out about one billion zlotys in areas hit by this month's heavy flooding, the head of the government's insurance supervision body (PUNU) told Rzeczpospolita daily.

"Our initial estimates show that all insurers offering non-life insurance will pay out about one billion zlotys of damages in areas hit by the floods," Danuta Walcerz was quoted as saying in the Monday edition of the newspaper.
Walcerz said Polish insurers should be able to withstand the financial burden of the payouts.
"This does not threaten the liquidity of non-life insurers as they have a combined 3.5 billion zlotys held in various short-term investments," she said.
Rzeczpospolita said Poland's four largest non-life insurers last week published early estimates of flood-related damages totalling 550 million zlotys.

Two weeks of heavy rains in the southern and western provinces resulted in Poland's worst flooding in centuries claiming 50 lives, swamping 5,400 sq km of land and more than a thousand towns and villages, of which 254 were still flooded.
But after a first flood wave a week ago the feared second wave has so far proved less damaging than expected.
